topic: The true cost of slow plumbing callbacks
hook_options: The call you're losing every Friday at 4pm
You're losing jobs in the first 3 rings
Plumbing owners: stop waiting until morning to call back
More ads won't fix your missed calls
3 reasons your missed calls go to competitors

cover.title: Stop waiting until morning to call back
cover.subtitle: See why the first plumber to answer gets the paycheck.

slides.heading: Leaks don't wait for business hours
slides.body: When a basement floods at 8 PM on a Tuesday, the homeowner calls down the list. They keep dialing until someone answers.
slides.tip: Call your own line after 5pm. What happens?

slides.heading: The five-minute window
slides.body: If you call back twenty minutes later, they have already booked the next shop on the list. But that's not even the expensive part...

slides.heading: Lost trust before the wrench turns
slides.body: Slow callbacks tell customers you are too busy for them. Even if you call them back first thing in the morning, they assume service will take days.
slides.tip: Check missed calls at 7am and 1pm daily.

slides.heading: Answering every ring keeps schedules full
slides.body: You don't need more ad spend. You just need someone to pick up when you're under a sink or driving to a supply house.

slides.heading: Quick capture recap
slides.body:
1. Callers dial down the list.
2. First to answer gets the job.
3. Speed beats a lower estimate every time.

caption:
When a homeowner has a plumbing emergency, the first shop that answers gets the job. 🛠️

Waiting until morning means handing that revenue straight to your competitors down the road.

How many missed calls do you think you had this week while your hands were under a sink?
image_prompt: A plumber kneeling beside a water heater in a residential basement, glancing down at a smartphone sitting on a toolbox
